title: 文件管理器鼠标右键菜单中没有PowerRename

fix_assessment.rationale: Current source has a plausible partial-registration repair gap, but the reporter's old per-user environment and the newer registry-workaround reports do not establish the affected registry state. Confirm the sentinel/handler-key condition before implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Repair missing PowerRename handler registrations when the sentinel remains
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: PowerRename's runtime registration helper trusts its ContextMenuRegistered sentinel and matching InprocServer32 path without checking the two declared context-menu handler keys. If either handler key is missing while the sentinel remains, EnsureRegistered can skip recreating it and Explorer may not show the command.
plan: Reproduce on a clean Windows 10 per-user installation and record the PowerRename sentinel, CLSID InprocServer32 path, and both declared handler keys without changing registry state.

If the partial-registration condition is confirmed, update runtime_shell_ext::EnsureRegistered to validate every declared contextMenuHandlerKeyPaths and repair missing or mismatched entries even when the sentinel and DLL path are present.
Add focused tests for missing handler keys with a retained sentinel, while preserving the intended per-user registration scope and avoiding HKLM mirroring.
verification: Use a disposable Windows 10 profile to confirm a clean current per-user install exposes PowerRename for single- and multi-file selections on its configured menu surface.
In a separate disposable test profile, simulate a missing handler key while retaining the sentinel and verify startup repairs the expected HKCU registration.
Verify normal and extended-only menu behavior and confirm no machine-wide registry writes are introduced.

confidence.rationale: Current upstream code directly shows that existing-sentinel repair does not validate PowerRename's declared handler keys, but no reporter registry snapshot proves that this state caused the missing menu.

issue_context.summary: PowerRename is missing from the Windows 10 context menu in an older per-user report, while later users report related missing shell entries and an unverified registry workaround.
known_information: The original report names PowerToys 0.96.1, Windows 10 build 19045, an elevated per-user installation, and says PowerRename is absent for both multiple-file and single-file selections.

A more recent commenter says PowerRename and File Locksmith are both missing and links a January 2026 diagnostic archive; another November 1 comment reports getting File Locksmith to appear after a claimed registry workaround: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/44232#issuecomment-6555308308
The latest comments describe copying user CLSID data into the machine registry. This is community-reported and unvalidated; it is not a supported or recommended fix.
Current PowerRename source declares two HKCU handler paths: AllFileSystemObjects\ShellEx\ContextMenuHandlers\PowerRenameExt and Directory\background\ShellEx\ContextMenuHandlers\PowerRenameExt.

Current runtime_shell_ext::EnsureRegistered checks the sentinel and InprocServer32 path, then checks a representative file association only when one is configured. PowerRename configures no representative association, and the existing-sentinel branch does not verify its declared handler paths before deciding whether to repair.
Related issue #51316 reports cross-tool context-menu duplication/visibility problems, but does not establish the cause of this Windows 10 PowerRename report.
inferences: A stale per-user registration sentinel with one or more missing handler keys could explain the missing PowerRename entry.
The later machine-wide registry workaround may reflect a different install-scope or shell-registration condition and does not prove that the original per-user issue has the same root cause.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is still open and the prior artifact's ownership rationale was unsupported: the saved report has no assignee. Current source provides a concrete repair-gap hypothesis in the existing-sentinel path, but the original report is from 0.96.1 and the latest workaround reports do not expose the relevant registry state. Reproduce on a clean current Windows 10 per-user install, inspect registrations read-only, and do not recommend importing HKCU keys into HKLM.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue body and all 13 comments, including the original per-user/elevated Windows 10 details, later missing-entry reports, and the November 1 community workaround.
Inspected current upstream PowerRename RuntimeRegistration.h and the shared shell_ext_registration.h implementation.

Confirmed the PowerRename spec declares two HKCU handler paths and no representative file association; the shared helper's existing-sentinel branch does not validate those handler paths before deciding to rewrite them.
Checked related issue #51316; it covers a broader provider/visibility report but is not a verified duplicate or fix for #44232.
Did not run or recommend the community registry-copy script or modify any installation.

judgment.rationale: The current helper has a concrete registration-repair gap that fits the symptom, but the live reports do not prove the affected registry state. Keep the design yellow and require a maintainer reproduction before implementation.
evidence: The original issue reports a missing PowerRename entry for single and multiple files on Windows 10 with a per-user installation.
Current PowerRename registration declares two handler paths, while the shared helper can skip rewriting them when the sentinel and CLSID server path are already present.
Later users report related missing entries, but their machine-scope workaround does not establish the original cause.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce on a clean current Windows 10 per-user install and verify whether an existing sentinel masks missing handler keys before approving the focused repair.

actions.label: Reproduce missing PowerRename registration on Windows 10

reproduce.title: Compare PowerRename menu visibility with per-user handler registrations
reproduce.version_requirement: Use current stable PowerToys on Windows 10 22H2 build 19045; compare against 0.96.1 only if the historical report must be reproduced.
prerequisites: Use a disposable Windows 10 profile with PowerRename enabled.
Prepare harmless single-file and multiple-file selections.
setup: Do not import registry data or run community scripts that copy HKCU registrations into HKLM.
Inspect existing registrations read-only; any partial-state simulation belongs only in a separate disposable test profile.
steps: Open Explorer's context menu for one file and for multiple files; test the normal menu and the extended menu when the PowerRename setting requires it.
Record the HKCU ContextMenuRegistered sentinel, the PowerRename CLSID InprocServer32 value, and the AllFileSystemObjects and Directory-background PowerRenameExt handler keys.

In a separate disposable test profile, simulate one missing handler key while retaining the sentinel and DLL path, then restart PowerToys and record whether registration is repaired and the menu entry appears.
reproduce.expected_result: PowerRename appears on the configured menu surface for supported selections; if a handler key is missing while the sentinel remains, startup restores it within the intended per-user registration scope.

summary: A current helper gap may leave PowerRename's menu entry missing when handler keys disappear but its per-user registration sentinel remains.
next_action: Reproduce the stale-sentinel case on Windows 10 before approving a focused registration repair.
